title: Senior iOS Developer (Mobile Commerce)
description:
About the role

We are looking for a Senior iOS Developer to build and improve a high-traffic retail shopping app. The app runs on the POQ app-commerce platform, with SAP Commerce Cloud as the e-commerce backend.

You will own key parts of the shopping journey, from product browsing and product detail pages to basket and checkout. The focus is a fast, stable app that handles large product catalogues, many images and peak trading traffic without slowing down or crashing.

What you'll do

* Build and maintain features in Swift across the shopping journey: product listing, product detail pages (PDP), search, basket, checkout and order history.
* Apply MVVM and clean architecture so screens stay testable, reusable and easy to change.
* Build checkout flows that handle complex orders, including splitting one order into several shipments based on store and warehouse stock.
* Design and maintain a clean networking layer for REST APIs, with typed models, error handling, retries and authentication.
* Use caching (NSCache, URLCache, on-disk storage) to keep PDP and catalogue screens fast.
* Optimise image loading and memory use for image-heavy product screens.
* Support offline use, persist product and cart data, and keep the cart in sync across devices and sessions.
* Find and fix crashes, memory leaks and slow screens using Instruments, Xcode Memory Graph and Firebase Crashlytics.
* Keep the UI smooth using Swift concurrency (async/await, actors), GCD and OperationQueue where each fits best.
* Own release delivery: certificates, provisioning profiles, TestFlight builds, App Store submission and CI/CD pipelines.
* Work with backend, design, QA and product teams on POQ configuration and SAP Commerce APIs.

What you'll bring

* **Swift and iOS SDK:**
  strong Swift, UIKit and SwiftUI, with a solid grasp of memory management (ARC, retain cycles, weak/unowned).
* **Architecture:**
  MVVM and MVC, and when to use each; clean architecture, coordinators, dependency injection and protocol-oriented design.
* **Networking:**
  URLSession, Codable, a modular API layer with request builders, error mapping, token refresh and retry logic.
* **Concurrency:**
  async/await, Task, actors and MainActor; GCD and OperationQueue for older code and dependent tasks.
* **Caching and persistence:**
  NSCache, URLCache and disk caching; Core Data, SwiftData or Realm; offline-first data and cart sync.
* **Image performance:**
  downsampling, prefetching, cell reuse and libraries such as Kingfisher or SDWebImage.
* **Debugging and monitoring:**
  Instruments (Time Profiler, Allocations, Leaks), Xcode Memory Graph and Firebase Crashlytics, including dSYM symbolication.
* **Release management:**
  certificates, App IDs, provisioning profiles, signing, TestFlight and App Store Connect review.
* **E-commerce experience:**
  at least one shipped retail or e-commerce app covering PDP, basket and checkout.
* **Engineering practice:**
  Git, unit and UI testing (XCTest), code review, and CI/CD with Xcode Cloud, Fastlane, Bitrise or GitHub Actions.

Nice to have

* Experience with the POQ app-commerce platform or a similar mobile commerce SDK (Shopify Mobile Buy SDK, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, commercetools).
* Working with SAP Commerce (OCC) APIs from a mobile app.
* Apple Pay, payment SDKs (Adyen, Stripe, Klarna) and secure storage with Keychain.
* Push notifications, deep links and universal links, and analytics tools (Firebase Analytics, Adobe, Amplitude).
* Combine, Swift Package Manager and modular app design.
* Accessibility (VoiceOver, Dynamic Type) and localisation for multiple markets.
* Some Android or Kotlin exposure.

Experience and qualifications

* 5–9 years in mobile development, including 4+ years building native iOS apps in Swift.
* At least 2 apps released to the App Store, ideally including a retail or e-commerce app with high daily traffic.
* Proven record of improving app stability (crash-free rate) and performance in production.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.
* Clear written and spoken English, and comfortable working with designers, backend engineers and product owners.
* Calm ownership of production issues and release deadlines, especially during peak trading.

title: Product Modernization - ACC+AJO Migration - Senior Technical Consultant
description:
**Who We Are**
WPP Enterprise Solutions designs, builds, and operates the growth systems that competitive businesses rely on. In a world where Al is reshaping how companies drive growth, we lead clients in business transformation and marketing modernization, connecting strategy directly to execution. Our 12,000 experts in engineering and platforms, commerce, consulting, content transformation, CRM, and CX work within a unified global operating unit across 40+ markets. WPP Enterprise Solutions works alongside best-in-class partners including Adobe, AWS, Braze, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Shopify, as well as innovators in AI, to deliver growth solutions tailored to the needs of our clients’ businesses. VML, part of WPP, supports WPP Enterprise Solutions by helping brands activate transformation through creativity and experience.
  
  
The opportunity
  
  
We seek Senior Consultants and Architects with deep, hands-on expertise in Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC), Adobe Campaign Standard (ACS), Adobe Experience Platform (AEP), and Adobe Journey Optimizer (AJO) to help enterprise customers modernize campaign and customer-journey programs. The role leads discovery, current-state assessment, target-state architecture, implementation, integration, testing, coexistence, cutover, and enablement. You will understand how customers use ACC or ACS today, identify use cases suited to AJO, and redesign them for AEP and AJO. Some functionality must be rebuilt, redesigned, retained, or handled through an integration or alternative solution. Candidates must explain product boundaries, assess feature and use-case fit, surface gaps early, and set realistic customer expectations. In AJO, a migrated use case lands on AJO Journeys (profile-centric, event-driven orchestration on AEP Real-Time Customer Profile) or AJO Orchestrated Campaigns (campaign-centric, batch, multi-step workflows on the AEP relational data store). Candidates must design and build on both, and recommend the right path per use case.
  
  
What you’ll be doing
  
  
- Assess and plan
- Lead discovery workshops with marketing, campaign operations, data, architecture, security, mobile, and IT stakeholders.
- Inventory the Campaign estate: use cases (batch, scheduled, transactional, event-triggered, real-time); assets (campaigns, workflows, audiences, deliveries, templates, content blocks, personalization, typologies, suppression rules, reporting); data (schemas and extensions, custom resources, relational data, targeting dimensions, identifiers, consent, opt-out, quarantine, bounce, engagement history); and infrastructure (on-premises or Managed Services hosting, network access, firewalls, file transfer, decommissioning needs).
- Reverse-engineer custom logic and document the business rules: technical and marketing workflows (query, enrichment, split, deduplication, reconciliation, update data, JavaScript code activities), custom JavaScript, JSSP, SOAP/JS API calls, SQL functions, stored procedures, custom relational structures, typology rules, input forms, web applications, landing pages, subscriptions, Message Center, Triggers/pipeline, offer logic, external accounts, APIs, middleware, and enterprise integrations.
- Map each use case and dependency to an AJO/AEP target pattern and classify it as reuse, redesign, rebuild, integrate, defer, or retain elsewhere. For custom logic, decide whether to re-express it in AEP/AJO (data model, Query Service, custom actions, external services), redesign or rebuild it separately, or retain it in Campaign.
- Choose the execution path per use case based on the target customer experience, not the shape of the source Campaign workflow. Use AJO Journeys when each profile should progress individually based on behaviour, events, or elapsed time, including many scheduled and recurring Campaign workflows rebuilt as Read Audience or business-event journeys. Use Orchestrated Campaigns for relational or multi-entity data, complex audience construction and enrichment, exact pre-send counts, and multi-level sending. Use action campaigns for simple scheduled or API-triggered sends. Document the rationale, combined patterns, and license prerequisites (e.g., the Journey Optimizer Campaigns package).
- Surface product-fit gaps and operational impacts before committing to scope or feature-parity claims. Advise when Campaign coexistence or another path fits better: Campaign v8 for ACC customers, or the ACS-to-Campaign v8 transition for ACS customers.
- Develop phased roadmaps, effort estimates, dependency plans, risks, and customer decision points.
- Architect and implement
- Design the AEP foundation: XDM schemas and field groups (profile, event, lookup); identity namespaces, identity resolution, profile enablement, and data relationships; datasets, sources, destinations, batch and streaming ingestion, and event design; data quality and governance; audience qualification and segmentation; and Query Service or other processing for transformation, aggregation, and enrichment.
- Replace common Campaign data patterns with AEP capabilities: Federated Audience Composition on Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Databricks, or other warehouses (closest to ACC Federated Data Access); computed attributes for profile-level aggregates; Data Distiller for scheduled SQL transformations; merge policies; and profile and segmentation guardrails.
- Design customer experiences and build AJO journeys and campaigns across batch and event-driven engagement: event- and segment-triggered orchestration, conditions, actions, custom actions, message content, personalization, and decisioning.
- Apply journey and campaign governance and optimization: business rules, frequency capping, quiet hours, journey priority and arbitration, conflict management, wave sending, content experimentation, and decisioning policies and rankings.
- Define security, access, permissions, governance, and operational controls.
- Build channels, integrations, and extensibility
- Configure AJO channels end to end: email, mobile and web push, in-app, web, code-based experiences, content cards, inbox, live activities, SMS/MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, LINE, and direct mail. Cover channel configurations, subdomains, API credentials, feedback webhooks, mobile app and SDK dependencies, channel-specific data and consent requirements, and template approval rules (e.g., WhatsApp/Meta).
- Connect messaging providers: native SMS providers (Sinch, Twilio, Infobip); bring-your-own-provider (BYOP) setups with provider payloads, inbound keyword handling, delivery receipts, and opt-in/opt-out webhooks and flows; and Channel Builder custom channels for non-native platforms or customer-owned gateways (e.g., regional or industry-specific providers), covering endpoint, authentication, throttling, payload structure, and monitoring.
- Design and build integrations using supported APIs, source connectors, file exchange, middleware, or Adobe solution integrations, including custom actions that call external systems from journeys (CRM, loyalty, order, recommendation, call-center, notification services) with request/response schemas, authentication (OAuth 2.0, API keys, mTLS), capping, throttling, retries, and error handling.
- Implement event and API-triggered patterns: unitary and business events, API-triggered and transactional campaigns, Interactive Message Execution / Journey and Campaign APIs, and streaming ingestion via HTTP API.
- Design and build Journeys (profile-centric)
- Select and configure the journey entry pattern per use case: unitary-event journeys for behavioural and transactional signals; audience qualification journeys on streaming audiences for real-time lifecycle moments; Read Audience journeys, one-shot or recurring with incremental read, for scheduled and batch-initiated programs that previously ran as recurring Campaign workflows; and business-event journeys that release an audience when an operational event occurs (e.g., a price drop or flight delay). Configure identity namespaces, reentrance and wait periods, exit criteria, and time zones.
- Build multi-step journeys where each customer progresses at their own pace: Wait activities; the Optimize activity for conditions, path targeting, and path experiments; reaction events on opens and clicks with timeout paths; Update Profile; Content Decision for offers; external data sources and custom actions for real-time lookups and system writebacks; and Jump activities to split complex programs into reusable journeys.
- Use supplemental identifiers (e.g., order, booking, subscription, or policy IDs), where enabled, to run one journey instance per entity and personalize with its attributes. Decide when per-entity use cases fit journeys versus orchestrated campaign multi-level sending.
- Support phased migration and coexistence from the journey canvas, including Adobe Campaign v7/v8 and ACS actions that let AJO orchestrate while Campaign transactional messaging delivers, until channels and content move to native AJO.
- Design within journey guardrails (one active instance per profile per journey, one Read Audience per journey and concurrent-run limits, entrance and processing throughput per sandbox, Jump and supplemental identifier restrictions, reaction event placement, custom action capping, and versioning impact on live profiles). Flag gaps to the customer early.
- Design and build Orchestrated Campaigns (relational)
- Design the data model with AEP relational (model-based) schemas, built manually or from a DDL or Excel upload: tables, primary and composite keys, version descriptors (e.g., lastmodified), ENUMs, data governance labels, identity fields mapped to identity namespaces, and links with correct cardinality (1-N, N-1, 1-1) to recipient and profile entities.
- Configure target dimensions, including the profile target dimension linking XDM profile and experience event data to relational data; decide what belongs in the profile store versus relational tables to avoid duplication.
- Set up Change Data Capture (CDC) ingestion from supported sources (e.g., Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP, Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Azure Databricks, Data Landing Zone): the \_change\_request\_type field for file-based loads, table logging for cloud warehouses, complete-record loads, deletion handling, and latency planning.
- Build multi-step canvases with targeting, flow control, and channel activities (Build, Read, and Save audience, Enrichment, Change dimension, Combine, Deduplication, Reconciliation, Split, Fork, AND-join, Wait, Alert), including multi-entity segmentation and multi-level sending (e.g., one message per booking, contract, subscription, account, or address linked to a profile) personalized with enriched relational attributes. Configure scheduling, recurring runs, and pre-send count validation.
- Design within orchestrated campaign guardrails (table count and schema size limits, daily change-volume limits, scalar-only audience attributes, uncached audience evaluation, permanent dataset table names, channel availability by license). Flag gaps to the customer early.
- Migrate data, logic, and personalization
- Translate the ACC/ACS relational data model to AEP: map recipient, custom, and relational tables to XDM profile, experience event, and lookup schemas, or to relational schemas for orchestrated campaigns; define primary and secondary identities, relationships, cardinality, and denormalization trade-offs.
- Migrate historical and operational data (profile attributes, subscriptions, consent and opt-out status, quarantine and bounce history, engagement data) via batch backfill, delta loads, and reconciliation reports. Map ACC/ACS denylist and subscription data to the AEP Consent and Preferences field group and AJO subscription lists; load quarantined and bounced addresses into the AJO suppression list via the Suppression API so blocked recipients stay blocked from day one.
- Rebuild Campaign workflow logic according to the chosen path. For journeys, express targeting as AEP audiences (batch, streaming, or edge) and computed attributes, recurring workflows as scheduled Read Audience journeys, and waits, splits, and tests as Wait and Optimize activities. For orchestrated campaigns, rebuild queries, enrichments, splits, union/intersection/exclusion, deduplication, change dimension, and reconciliation as canvas activities. Use Query Service (SQL/CTAS) jobs or source dataflows for scheduled imports/exports and data preparation. Move logic neither canvas supports (JavaScript activities and code, SQL code, loops, file manipulation) to the source system, Query Service or Data Distiller, or external services.
- Re-architect lifecycle programs (welcome, onboarding, renewal, win-back, abandonment) built in Campaign as chained or recurring workflows into journeys, replacing workflow-based state tracking (custom flags, prior-recipient exclusion lists, wait loops) with journey state, reentrance rules, and exit criteria.
Convert ACC/ACS HTML content, templates, and personalization ( scripting, JavaScript in content, personalization blocks, conditional content) to AJO content templates and Handlebars/PQL: helper functions, conditional and dynamic content, expression and visual fragments, and decisioning outputs. Validate matching output with seed and test profiles.- Map Message Center, Triggers/pipeline, and other transactional or signal-driven flows to AJO unitary-event journeys or API-triggered campaigns, and typology, pressure, and fatigue rules to AJO business rules, frequency capping, suppression rules, and quiet hours.
- Migrate ACC Interaction offer logic (catalogs, categories, eligibility rules, weights, typology and presentation rules, inbound and outbound environments) to AJO Decisioning: decision items,
collections, selection strategies, ranking formulas or AI models, and capping. Confirm whether the customer is licensed for Decisioning or legacy Offer Decisioning.
  
  

* Rebuild Campaign landing pages, subscription and preference centers, web and survey forms, ACC web applications, and JSSP pages as AJO landing pages, subscription lists, or customer-owned web front ends connected through AEP APIs, writing consent and preferences back to AEP.
* Deliver, test, and transition
* Establish development, test/stage, and production delivery practices with Git version control and a sandbox strategy. Support controlled promotion and release management with AEP sandbox tooling packages (schemas, audiences, journeys, content templates), journey versioning, simulation, and dry-run checks before publishing.
* Build requirements-traceable test strategies and plans covering data and identity validation, audience counts, journey logic, personalization, rendering, API behavior, consent, suppression, channel delivery, and reporting.
* Design dual-run and cutover plans, synchronizing and reconciling consent, opt-outs, quarantine, bounces, profile data, and engagement history as needed.
* Plan deliverability readiness and email domain migration: subdomain delegation (full or CNAME), SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, one-click List-Unsubscribe headers, Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender requirements, IP pools and strategy, ramp-up and warm-up, bounce, quarantine, suppression, and opt-in/opt-out handling, and operational monitoring and reporting.
* Rebuild Campaign reporting and tracking with AJO built-in journey and campaign reports, Customer Journey Analytics where licensed, and Query Service on AJO system datasets (message feedback, email tracking, journey step events). Agree with the customer which ACC reports, KPIs, and tracking logs need equivalents.
* Define measurable launch and migration acceptance criteria; support business validation, production readiness, go-live, stabilization, and continuous improvement.
* Hand over with implementation documentation, architecture diagrams, reproducible data mapping specifications, runbooks, testing evidence, and operational and support materials; coach customer teams on the AJO operating model, AEP concepts, changed workflows, new responsibilities, and adoption needs.

What we want from you
  
  

* Adobe Campaign Classic - ACC v7/v8 architecture and implementation, including mid-sourcing, FFDA/Snowflake on v8, and Federated Data Access. Campaign data model and XML schema extensions; workflows and technical workflows; targeting and enrichment; deliveries, templates, personalization, typologies, and rules; transactional messaging (Message Center) and Triggers where applicable; tracking and delivery data; JSSP, web applications, SOAP APIs, packages, and external accounts; customizations and integrations.
* Adobe Campaign Standard - ACS campaign and workflow design; audiences, deliveries, templates, personalization, channel configuration, data resources, imports/exports, APIs, and consent and subscription practices. Assessing ACS implementations and translating requirements to AEP/AJO design.
* Adobe Experience Platform - XDM modeling; schemas, datasets, identity namespaces and identity resolution; Real-Time Customer Profile concepts; batch and streaming ingestion; sources and destinations; segmentation; Query Service/data transformation; governance and consent considerations; sandboxes and environment strategy.
* Adobe Journey Optimizer - Journey and campaign design (action, API-triggered, orchestrated); unitary, business, and audience-based patterns; journey activities, conditions

What we can offer you
  
  
Alongside the opportunity to work with some of the most exciting brands around the world, we’ll also prioritise your career development and help you grow your skills. We’ll empower you to make a difference, allow you to be yourself, and respect who you are.
  
  
Our culture thrives on our core values, designed for impact-driven individuals: Heart, Brains and Courage.
  
  
We lead with
**Heart**
, fostering empathy and trust where genuine connections and human-centric work flourish.

**Brains**
for innovation, valuing relentless curiosity and collaborative intelligence to solve complex challenges.
  
  
And we champion
**Courage**
, inspiring you to speak up, embrace experimentation, and advocate for bold solutions that push our thinking to be better than yesterday.

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence and world-class partnerships – all united by our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com.

title: Head of Voice AI Development
description:
You'll own voice AI at JoyzAI. All of it. The real\-time pipeline (audio in, speech understood, LLM reasoning, tools called, speech out), the telephony that gets the call connected, the platform a client uses to configure and run their agent, and the webhooks and CRM plumbing that turn a call into a lead. It's a working product with real clients on it today. Your job is to take it from working to something we'd bet the company on, and to build the team that keeps it that way.
 



 This is a head\-of role at a company of under 15 people, which makes it a player\-coach job. You set the technical direction for voice: what we build on, what we buy, what we rip out. And you write a lot of the code yourself. When a call stutters, drops, or talks over the customer, you're the one who finds out why, fixes it at the root, and changes the system so it can't happen again. When a client wants an agent that does something we've never done, you decide whether the platform can, and then you make it so.
 



  





**What you'll do** 




  





**Own the voice stack** 



* Set the architecture and roadmap for the real\-time calling pipeline: telephony ↔ audio streaming ↔ speech/real\-time models ↔ tool calls ↔ speech out, with latency you can't feel.
* Own the hard voice problems, with opinions earned in production: turn\-taking and barge\-in, silence and voicemail detection, noise and echo, language switching mid\-call (English ↔ Hinglish ↔ regional), and graceful recovery when a model or carrier hiccups.
* Make the build\-vs\-buy calls across STT/TTS, real\-time LLMs, VAD, and telephony carriers. Run the evaluations, own the vendor relationships, decide what we build on next, and know when it's time to switch.
* Design non\-blocking tool calling inside live calls (lookups, bookings, CRM writes) so the agent never goes silent or loses the thread.
* Define what "good" means for a voice agent: the quality bar, the evaluation framework, the test harness. We should know a change made agents better before a client tells us.



  





**Build the platform around the calls** 



* Own the Node.js/Express services and APIs that have to hold up as call volume grows: call orchestration, queueing, webhooks, retries, recording and transcript storage.
* Own the product around the calls: agent configuration (tasks, behaviour, guardrails, AI config), call logs and transcripts, analytics, and bulk\-calling campaign controls.
* Wire calls into the rest of the platform: CRM contacts and tickets, WhatsApp follow\-ups after a call, calendar and booking integrations, Google Sheets and Meta lead\-form ingestion.
* Keep the Angular frontends our team and clients use (the agent configurator, the inbox, the call review screens) clean and usable, whether you're writing them or reviewing them.



  





**Reliability, cost \& scale** 



* Instrument everything: time\-to\-first\-word, per\-call latency breakdowns, drop rates, tool\-call failures, model cost per minute. Own the dashboards that tell us something's wrong before a client does.
* Treat cost per minute as a number you're accountable for. Bring it down without hurting quality: model choice, streaming strategy, caching, carrier routing.
* Own production. Debug incidents on real client calls, reproduce them, fix them at the root, and build the incident and on\-call practice so the next one gets caught faster.



  





**Lead the team** 



* Build and lead the voice engineering team. Hire, set the bar, review the code, and make the engineers around you better.
* Own the engineering standard for voice: architecture decisions, code quality, documentation, what ships and what doesn't.
* Pair with the prompt engineer and customer success on what the platform needs for agents to behave well: new tool types, better fallbacks, a proper test harness for prompts.
* Be the technical authority in front of clients on the hard deployments, the ones where the answer isn't in the docs yet.
* Turn what you learn from client deployments into reusable platform capability, so the next voice agent takes hours to stand up, not days.



  





 Roughly 60% of your time is hands\-on: architecting, coding, debugging live calls, shipping. The other 40% is leading: the team, the roadmap, model and vendor decisions, and the client conversations where the platform's direction gets decided. That ratio shifts toward leading as the team grows, but you never stop being able to open the code and fix it yourself.
 



  





**What we're looking for** 




  





 Three things are non\-negotiable. Please apply only if you meet all three. They're the first thing we screen for.
 



  




* **You have successfully deployed voice AI agents to production, and owned them there.** 
 Not a demo, not a hackathon, not a pilot that quietly ended. A system where real customers spoke to an AI over a phone line or live audio stream, at real volume, for months, and it stayed in production because it worked. You owned the pipeline end to end: streaming audio, speech and real\-time models, latency, interruptions, the failures at 2am, the cost. In our first conversation we'll ask what you shipped, how many calls it handled, what broke, and what you did about it. Come with specifics. Experience at a Voice AI company is a strong signal.



  




* **You can build the whole thing yourself.** 
 Backend services, APIs, real\-time transport, databases, and a frontend a client can use without a walkthrough. You've done this as an individual contributor and you can still do it. A head of voice who can't debug the socket is not who we're hiring.



  




* **You've set the technical direction for a voice product before.** 
 As a founding engineer, tech lead, architect, or head of engineering. The title matters less than the fact that people looked to you for what to build and how, and you were right often enough that the product worked.



  





 Beyond that, we don't care much about degrees or years. We care that you can:
 



  




* Work fluently across the MEAN stack — MongoDB, Express, Angular, Node.js — with TypeScript throughout.
* Design and debug real\-time systems: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming audio, event\-driven architectures, queues.
* Integrate with telephony/SIP providers and messaging APIs (WhatsApp Business API) and handle their quirks in production.
* Work with LLM APIs, tool/function calling, and speech models, and reason about latency, cost, and failure modes, not just accuracy.
* Design MongoDB data models and APIs for a multi\-tenant SaaS: contacts, conversations, tickets, workflows, role\-based access.
* Hire well, review well, and explain a hard technical call to a founder or a client in plain language.
* Measure and profile before you optimise, write code others can read, and document what you built.



  





 Nice to have: deep experience with real\-time voice frameworks or APIs (OpenAI Realtime, LiveKit, Pipecat, or similar); Indian telephony providers; Hinglish or Indic speech models; GCP/AWS at scale; having scaled a voice product from its first client to serious call volume; having built a voice team from scratch.
 



  





 Full\-time, on\-site in Noida.
 



  





**Why JoyzAI?** 




  





 ✨ Utmost freedom and autonomy — voice AI is yours. Make the decisions, set the direction, do it the way you think is best. We will only suggest.
 



 ✨ Complete responsibility. You are the taskmaster. Take responsibility for it.
 



 ✨ Top\-of\-the\-market pay – we reward high performance with the best packages.
 



 ✨ 5\-day working – weekends are yours to recharge.
 



 ✨ Work from office in Noida – collaborate, learn, and grow with a passionate team.
 



 ✨ High\-growth startup – opportunity to see first hand how AI brings change and be a part of that.
